note: #932, the cold twin of #909. Start's primary attachment and attachExtra validated the shape of their network name and asked ownership of neither, where Attach asks both since #909. The question is asked once at the entry of Start over the whole of Spec.Attachments, before anything is sent to the runtime, so it covers the primary interface, the extra NICs (Start is attachExtra's only caller) and the restart branch alike. Proven through the injectable runner, not against a running Incus. Two things this spec does NOT hold, so that nobody reads its count as a full proof. The second mutation is the same find/replace as the first with a different judge: it removes the whole guard, and it is the third mutation, which narrows the loop to the primary attachment, that actually proves the extra NICs are covered. And no mutation here anchors the guard's POSITION: move the loop below the Inspect and all of them still apply and still bite, while 'before anything is sent to the runtime' would have become false. That position is held by the tests, not by this spec: TestStartRefusesANetworkOutsideThePrefix requires len(f.calls)==0, and TestStartRefusesAForeignNetworkOnAnExtraNIC requires that no init and no start were emitted. Two measured facts that belong with this guard and are not mutations here. ownedAttachments is called twice, by Start at its entry and by attachExtra at its own, and only the first is measured: deleting the attachExtra call leaves TestStartRefusesAForeignNetworkOnAnExtraNIC green, measured by hand on 2026-11-14, because Start's call already refused the boot. That inner call is defence in depth for a caller added later, and no mutation can express 'a second caller appears'. And before this lot, a bad network on an extra NIC was refused by attachExtra AFTER init and start, and that return path does not call abandonStart, so the instance stayed running while the pack published FailedState. The entry call removes the name-caused version of that; the runtime-caused version stands and is getting its own issue. A machine already sitting on a foreign network also cannot have that NIC removed through the API, since Detach refuses the network; terminate still works, because the instance carries our label, so nothing is stuck.
